source_refs.note: Topic 2.5.3 Importing and Using Libraries (PDF 48-49, printed 45-46). 'Import datetime' is printed with a capital I. The list-comprehension answer is general Python; flagged.

blocks.text: Libraries are pre-built toolkits used through import. Three standard libraries are shown: random for random numbers, datetime for dates and times, and statistics for calculations such as the mean.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
import random
number = random.randint(1, 10)
print("The random number is:", number)

import datetime
print("Current date and time:", datetime.datetime.now())

import statistics
data = [23, 45, 67, 89, 12, 44, 56]
print("The mean value is:", statistics.mean(data))

random helps in games, simulations or picking a lucky-draw winner; datetime helps with logging events and reminders; statistics finds the mean, median and mode. Import only what you need; more libraries are listed at https://docs.python.org/3/ (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: What is the mean of the data list in the example?
Class activity: use random to make a list of 10 numbers from 1 to 50 and statistics to print their mean.
blocks.explanation: import random, statistics; nums = [random.randint(1, 50) for _ in range(10)]; print(statistics.mean(nums)). The mean changes on every run because the numbers are random.

items: import a library to use it: random.randint, datetime.datetime.now, statistics.mean (data mean 48).
